text: According to class nominalism, what is the property of being red?
choices: The class of all red things; to be red is just to be a member of that class.
A primitive resemblance among red things, which need not form any class.
Simply the applicability of the predicate 'red', with no worldly entity involved.
A universal, redness, wholly present in each distinct red thing.
explanation: Class nominalism identifies a property with the class of its instances. The tempting distractor is resemblance nominalism (option 1), which grounds redness in a primitive resemblance relation among particulars rather than in class membership; note too that class nominalism does not fully escape abstracta, since classes are themselves abstract objects.
